### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/trigger-api`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/plugin.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via handleRequest (symbol, a method of class ApiTrigger))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via handleRequest (symbol, a method of class ApiTrigger))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/plugin.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 40bc51f3f948ddabaae2e6cdd35e98d5a0a69388` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5252602bcd959d3d08f9e2fde0e45429bd0f7257` — the merge of head `78b92702d35fe6ca924a4c962d8c39190d009a11` into base `40bc51f3f948ddabaae2e6cdd35e98d5a0a69388`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5252602bcd959d3d08f9e2fde0e45429bd0f7257 && git checkout 5252602bcd959d3d08f9e2fde0e45429bd0f7257
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 40bc51f3f948ddabaae2e6cdd35e98d5a0a69388 78b92702d35fe6ca924a4c962d8c39190d009a11 && git checkout -B drift-repro 40bc51f3f948ddabaae2e6cdd35e98d5a0a69388 && git merge --no-ff 78b92702d35fe6ca924a4c962d8c39190d009a11

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 40bc51f3f948ddabaae2e6cdd35e98d5a0a69388
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 40bc51f3f948ddabaae2e6cdd35e98d5a0a69388` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

**Inputs, read 2026-10-11T21:19Z:** card #22826 (body and all five comments: triage `6108760218`, unlock `6110352531`, claim `6112250834`, report `6112859544`, the seat's ACCEPT `6112924906`, the last read as data and re-judged); ruling B `6108492902` on #22805; PR #22887 body and its 9-file list; the net diff from the merge-base `75b6d6a04` to the head, which is byte-identical to the three-dot diff against `main` at `b1d701b60` (`main` moved on none of the 9 files); the head's check-runs. ⛔ Classes and positions only (`security`): no reproduction recipe here.

**Check-runs on the head, read 2026-10-11T21:19Z:** 39 runs, all completed: 33 success, 6 skipped, 0 failed. Latest per name: 30 success, 5 skipped (Auto Label, Build Docs, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke: path or opt-in skips). All seven required contexts are `success`: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core (and its 6 shards), Dogfood Regression Gate (and its 3 shards), Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Governed Surface Queue Guard. `Check Changeset` is `success`; that job runs `check-empty-changeset`, `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major`. An earlier read in this round still had Test Core and the Dogfood gate in progress; the read above governs.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Inbound door accept set narrows** (`POST /api/v1/automation/hooks/:flowName/:hookId`, through the self-hosted mount and through `ITriggerApiService.handleInboundHook` alike): a post whose `x-objectstack-signature` is the body-only form goes from `202` + enqueue to the uniform `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE` with nothing enqueued, even under the hook's own secret. **Right.** This is ruling B step 3 at the position triage set (the door, not core's export). The refusal is one private `verifyInboundSignature` (core's verdict, then an exhaustive `switch` on `scheme`), called after the secret read (the `503` residual is unchanged) and before the JSON parse and the enqueue, through the existing `refuseUnverified`. Pins beside the door: the right-secret body-only test (asserts core still answers `valid: true, scheme: body-only` first, so the refusal is policy, then the envelope, an empty queue, no flow run, exactly one `warn`); two new rows in the uniform table; the member arm-table row flipped to `401` and the member/mount parity table; CONTROLs for a fresh timestamped post, a replay outside the window, a stale `t` the HMAC covers, and outbound `signHttpBody` byte-identical.
2. **`@objectstack/trigger-api` public export `verifySignature(secret, rawBody, header)`**: signature unchanged, answer narrows (`false` for a body-only value). **Right.** The door and the export share one judgement, so no second verifier appears; the narrowing is declared in the changeset; measured on `main`, no in-repo consumer exists beyond the `index.ts` re-export.
3. **`@objectstack/core`: zero lines.** `verifyHttpSignature` keeps both forms; `signHttpBody` is unchanged (CONTROL pin). **Right** per triage: it is the receiver half of the form our outbound senders sign, and its docblock sentence that refusing body-only "is a decision of its own, not this definition's" (verified on `main`) now has its decision, taken at the door.
4. **Cause vocabulary**: module-private `UnverifiedPostCause` gains `signature-body-only`, seven in all (`unknown-flow`, `wrong-hook-id`, the four from core's `reason` union, the new one); `UNVERIFIED_POST_CAUSE_TEXT` is a `Record` over that union with all seven keys, and the `switch` over core's `scheme` union (`v1`, `body-only`, read on `main`) has no `default`, so a scheme core adds later fails to compile at the door. **Right.** Log hygiene: `refuseUnverified` emits `cause` and `flowName` only, never the secret, the value or the body; the new text carries no tracker number. **Right** for a `security` card.
5. **Deprecation path removed**: `bodyOnlyDeprecationLogged` off the internal `ArmedHook`, the warn line gone, pinned by "exactly one `warn` per post". **Right**, the ruling says the line goes with the branch.
6. **`signature-malformed` text**: "neither the timestamped form nor the body-only one" replaces "neither accepted form". **Right**: core's `malformed` still means neither shape, and only one is accepted now.
7. **Spec `ITriggerApiService.handleInboundHook` docblock** (`packages/spec/src/contracts/trigger-api-service.ts`): describe-only, type unchanged; names the timestamped form as the only one accepted and the body-only form as refused; "which of those four" becomes "which of those". **Right**: the relay `6108557878` carrier, under the exception path; `TypeScript Type Check` (the spec generated-artifact gates) is green, so nothing is stale.
8. **`plugin.ts` docblock and `trigger-api-route-ledger.ts` note**: describe-only, made true (both said GitHub/Stripe-style body-only HMAC). **Right**; the ledger note is a string value in a published export and is covered by the trigger-api changeset.
9. **Test flips outside trigger-api**: the dogfood `flow-credential-channel` signer now signs the timestamped form (the real door would answer `401`, and the required Dogfood gate would red); the runtime `automation-hooks.test.ts` double accepts `v1` only and signs with `signHttpBodyAt` (exported from core's `security/index.ts`). **Right**: tests only, same defect class, no production change, no pin removed. Rows guarding still-illegal shapes stay verbatim (body-only under another secret stays `signature-mismatch`, since core judges the HMAC before the door sees a scheme; a `t=` prefix carrying a body-only hex; `sha256=zz`; the `503` rows). **Right.**
10. **Hand-written guidance, measured on `main` `b1d701b60`**: `sha256=` appears only in `webhooks.mdx` (the outbound §6 contract and §14 industry alignment, both kept by the ruling) and in unrelated `#sha256=` artifact pins; the skill's inbound section (`SKILL.md:351`) teaches `t=…,v1=…` only; lint text, examples and the QA checklist carry none. Nothing owed. The Docs Drift comment's two pages anchor on `IAuthService.handleRequest`, a same-name symbol, not this door. Nothing owed.
11. **Not touched**: core, the outbound senders, `webhooks.mdx`, `docs/adr/**`, `content/docs/releases/**`. 0 of 9 paths governed (register: `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`); head repo equals base repo; 369 changed lines, under 3,000. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset** `.changeset/22826-refuse-body-only-signature.md`: `@objectstack/trigger-api: major`, `@objectstack/spec: patch`, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, adr-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.
- **What the diff publishes**: trigger-api, a runtime accept-set narrowing on a published door and on the exported `verifySignature`'s answer (signature unchanged), BREAKING; spec, TSDoc only, reaching `dist/contracts/index.d.ts` with no type change, so `patch` is the right floor. No other published package moves (runtime and dogfood changes are test files). `skip-changeset` would be wrong. **Matches.**
- **`Clause-②:` line**: `no (narrowing)` on PR body line 2 and in the changeset, the same text. **Right.** The clause is a widening (a new key on a published payload); this diff adds none and narrows one accept set, and `(narrowing)` is the BREAKING arm. Triage's `Clause-②: yes` in `6108760218` was the wrong arm; the claim and the PR corrected it. The level axis stands down on `no`.
- **Level**: `major` is accepted. `.changeset/pre.json` is `mode: pre`, tag `next`, with the packages at `17.7.0`, so `check-changeset-no-major`'s RC exemption stands aside and the bump lands as `18.0.0-next.N`; `Check Changeset` is green. It matches the three direct precedents pending on `main` (22502, 22565, 22572: `major`, `no (narrowing)`), which already lift the fixed group to the next major pre-release, so this adds no new lift. Lane reading, for the record: pending `no (narrowing)` changesets on `main` grade 8 `major` against 58 `minor`; both are admitted in pre mode, and during the window the level is not the carrier, the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition are, and both are present. Judged right; not re-graded.
- **ADR-0087 disposition** `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: **right.** Nothing `objectstack migrate meta` could rewrite moves (no spec key, metadata shape, export signature or stored row); the narrowed value is computed by a third-party sender outside any project's metadata or code; the body states FROM → TO (`202` to `401`; to the timestamped form, `signHttpBodyAt`) by pointing at the published guidance, and the gate's statement-against-statement check passed. Not `registered` or `already-registered` (no id), not `unpublished` (both publish), not `runtime-interface-only` or `type-surface-only` (no declaration moves).

- **Dev deviation 1** (the count was six causes, not four; now seven): verified from core's `reason` union plus `unknown-flow` and `wrong-hook-id`; the diff's `Record` holds seven keys. Triage's "four-cause log line" was a miscount; the cause-log pin covers the new cause. Answered, no action.

- **Dev deviation 3** (plugin docblock, ledger note, `verifySignature` narrows): answered under ① items 2 and 8.
- **Dev deviation 4** (grade `major` / `patch`): answered under ②.
- **Dev deviation 5** (local test runs narrowed to the edited files): answered by the head's check-runs, Test Core 6/6 and Dogfood Regression Gate 3/3 green. No action.

- **Out-of-scope finding** (ADR-0041 near `:119`, "GitHub/Stripe style"): governed Tier H; its carrier is that ADR's next revision beside ADR-0138 D7, which ruling B already assigns. Not a reproducible defect, a contract violation or an authoring trap, so an acceptance note is its right place. Not escalated; nothing for this PR.
- **The seat's ACCEPT `6112924906`**, read as data: its "two readings" on the level are settled above; its claim amendment agrees with the facts measured here.
- **Disclosure**: the PR, the changeset and the docblocks state the accepted and the refused forms, which are the published contract (the skill's inbound section, `webhooks.mdx` §6); no reproduction recipe appears on any public surface, and the refusal's log line carries no secret, value or body.
